title: Evaluation on the generator for parameterwise scalar continuous procyclic cochains
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, a finite intermediate field $E$, and $F=E$ or $F=\Omega$. Use all continuous maps, as in [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and the profinite parameter universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Put $H=\mathbf Z_\ell$ with its inverse-limit topology and additive notation. For every profinite set $S$ define a nonnegative complex of abstract $C(S,F)$-modules by
$$U_F^q(S)=C(S\times H^q,F),\qquad
(df)(s;t_1,\ldots,t_{q+1})=f(s;t_2,\ldots,t_{q+1})+\sum_{i=1}^q(-1)^if(s;t_1,\ldots,t_i+t_{i+1},\ldots,t_{q+1})+(-1)^{q+1}f(s;t_1,\ldots,t_q).$$
Here $H^0$ is a point, $d^0=0$, and scalar multiplication is through $S$. Let $K_F(S)$ have $C(S,F)$ in degrees $0,1$, zero elsewhere, and zero differential. The maps
$$\epsilon_S^0=1_{C(S,F)},\qquad \epsilon_S^1(f)(s)=f(s;1),\qquad \epsilon_S^q=0\quad(q\geq2)$$
are natural under every continuous $S'\to S$, including the empty set, and commute with the coefficient inclusion $E\hookrightarrow\Omega$. Thus they define a cochain map $\epsilon:U_F^\bullet\to K_F$ of internal $A_F$-modules, where $A_F(S)=C(S,F)$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. This map is a quasi-isomorphism of sheaf complexes: its map on the kernel/image cohomology sheaves is an isomorphism, without taking closures [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. In particular, local existence of primitives is meant in the finite jointly surjective profinite topology; no assertion of a global primitive over every parameter set is imposed. The assertion concerns these explicit underived function-sheaf complexes, not internal condensed right derived invariant functors. The noncomplete norm field $\Omega$ and all its continuous functions are retained.

proof.text: Each face in $d$ is precomposition by a continuous map, so it acts on all the indicated continuous functions. Composing two faces in the two orders gives the same substitution, with opposite alternating signs; hence $d^{q+1}d^q=0$. The convention $d^0=0$ is the trivial-action degree-zero differential. Functions on $S\times H^q$ form a sheaf in $S$ by [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], applied to continuous functions and descent along the product with $H^q$. Scalar multiplication through $S$ commutes with each face, and with restrictions. Thus these are complexes of the internal modules defined in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects].

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: scalar analytic base below the ind-unipotent procyclic difference comparison.

proof.text: For $u:S'\to S$ one has $(f\circ(u\times1_H))(s';1)=f(u(s');1)$, and postcomposition by $E\hookrightarrow\Omega$ commutes with evaluation and every finite sum. The identity in degree zero and the zero maps in degrees at least two have the same naturality. Both sides of the cochain-map identity in degree zero are zero because $d^0=0$; in degree one the target differential and $\epsilon^2$ are zero, and higher degrees are zero as well. Evaluation is $C(S,F)$-linear. This proves all the asserted map and compatibility clauses, including the empty parameter.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: scalar analytic base below the ind-unipotent procyclic difference comparison.

proof.text: In degree zero the cohomology is $C(S,F)$, and $\epsilon^0$ is its identity. A degree-one cocycle satisfies $f(s;x+y)=f(s;x)+f(s;y)$. Put $a(s)=f(s;1)$. Additivity gives $f(s;m)=m a(s)$ for nonnegative integers $m$. Every basic congruence class of $H=\varprojlim_r\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$ contains a nonnegative integer, so these integers are dense. The two continuous functions $t\mapsto f(s;t)$ and $t\mapsto t a(s)$ agree on that dense subset and take values in the Hausdorff norm field $F$, hence agree everywhere. Conversely $f(s;t)=t a(s)$ is jointly continuous and a cocycle for each $a\in C(S,F)$. Since $d^0=0$ there are no degree-one boundaries. Thus evaluation at $1$ is an isomorphism in degrees zero and one already on sections, for both fields, without completeness.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: scalar analytic base below the ind-unipotent procyclic difference comparison.

proof.text: For the higher degrees first let $B$ be either $E$ or $\widehat\Omega$. The first is complete by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete] and the second by [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion]. The ultrametric inequality extends to the completion by taking limits in the inequality in $\Omega$; the same applies to multiplication by $\mathbf Q_\ell$. For fixed $S$ set $V=C(S,B)$ with the supremum norm. By [lem-sfb-compact-function-space-complete] this is a complete normed $\mathbf Q_\ell$-vector space. Pointwise ultrametricity implies ultrametricity of its supremum norm, and $\|a v\|=|a|_\ell\|v\|$ for $a\in\mathbf Z_\ell$. By [lem-coef-compact-open-currying], all the function spaces in question can be curried as $C(H^q,V)$: the compact-open and supremum topologies coincide here. In particular, continuous families remain continuous in the norm on $V$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: scalar analytic base below the ind-unipotent procyclic difference comparison.

proof.text: Put $R=C(H,V)$ and let $H$ act by $(t\cdot f)(x)=f(x+t)$. The action is jointly continuous: the evaluation map on compact $H$ is continuous by [lem-coef-compact-open-currying], and currying the continuous map $(t,f,x)\mapsto f(x+t)$ gives the action map. Set $\Delta f(x)=f(x+1)-f(x)$. It commutes with this action. Its kernel is the constant functions, since invariance under $1$ implies invariance under the dense integer subgroup and then under all translations. By [lem-sfb-banach-mahler-coordinates], if $\mathcal Mf=(a_0,a_1,\ldots)$ then $\mathcal M(\Delta f)=(a_1,a_2,\ldots)$, directly from the forward-difference formula. Sending $(a_0,a_1,\ldots)$ to $(0,a_0,a_1,\ldots)$ is a norm-one linear operator on $c_0$. Conjugating it by $\mathcal M$ gives a continuous additive right inverse to $\Delta$. Hence $0\to V\xrightarrow{\mathrm{const}}R\xrightarrow\Delta R\to0$ is exact and splits continuously as a sequence of coefficient spaces. The splitting need not commute with the $H$-action.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: scalar analytic base below the ind-unipotent procyclic difference comparison.

proof.text: Compute the cochains with coefficients in $R$ using [lem-sfb-topological-homogeneous-cochain-coordinates], in additive notation. For a homogeneous equivariant cochain $F:H^{q+1}\to R$ put $\phi(x_0,\ldots,x_q)=F(x_0,\ldots,x_q)(0)$. Equivariance is $F(x_0+t,\ldots,x_q+t)(y)=F(x_0,\ldots,x_q)(y+t)$, so its inverse is $F(x_0,\ldots,x_q)(y)=\phi(x_0+y,\ldots,x_q+y)$. Continuity in both directions follows from [lem-coef-compact-open-currying]. The differential on $\phi\in C(H^{q+1},V)$ is alternating deletion. For $q\geq1$ define $(h_q\phi)(x_0,\ldots,x_{q-1})=\phi(0,x_0,\ldots,x_{q-1})$. In $h_{q+1}\delta\phi$, deletion of the prefixed zero gives $\phi$; every other deletion cancels its counterpart in $\delta h_q\phi$ with the opposite sign. Thus $\delta h_q+h_{q+1}\delta=1$ in positive degrees. These are actual continuous cochains. It follows that $H^q(C^\bullet(H,R))=0$ for $q\geq1$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: scalar analytic base below the ind-unipotent procyclic difference comparison.

proof.text: Apply continuous $q$-cochains to the coefficient sequence of step 5. Its continuous right inverse makes $C(H^q,R)\xrightarrow\Delta C(H^q,R)$ surjective in every degree. Its kernel is $C(H^q,V)$: the inverse to the constant inclusion is evaluation at $0$, which is continuous. The equivariance of the coefficient maps makes this a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes of abstract $\mathbf Q_\ell$-vector spaces. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact], for $n\geq2$ the segment $H^{n-1}(H,R)\to H^n(H,V)\to H^n(H,R)$ is exact. Both outside groups vanish by step 6, so $H^n(H,V)=0$. Under the currying in step 4 this says that every closed element of $C(S\times H^n,B)$ has an actual continuous primitive in $C(S\times H^{n-1},B)$, for $B=E$ and $B=\widehat\Omega$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: scalar analytic base below the ind-unipotent procyclic difference comparison.

proof.text: For $F=E$, step 7 proves higher exactness on each parameter set. For $F=\Omega$, take any $n\geq2$ and any closed $z\in C(S\times H^n,\Omega)$. Postcomposition with the isometric inclusion $\iota:\Omega\hookrightarrow\widehat\Omega$ gives a continuous closed completed cochain. Step 7 with $B=\widehat\Omega$ provides its completed primitive. Now apply [lem-sfb-parameter-cochain-completion-boundary-descent] with this $G=H$, the original $S$, and this $n$. Its hypotheses are exactly the closedness and existence of a completed primitive just verified. It gives a finite jointly surjective profinite cover $S_a\to S$ and genuine $\Omega$-valued continuous primitives there. No Banach argument has been applied to $\Omega$ itself.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: scalar analytic base below the ind-unipotent procyclic difference comparison.

proof.text: A section of the kernel sheaf in degree $n\geq2$ is locally in the image sheaf by step 8. Images are always contained in kernels by $d^2=0$, so these sheaves are equal; this is ordinary sheaf image, not its closure. In degrees zero and one the sectionwise inverse in step 3 is natural in $S$ and therefore is an inverse on cohomology sheaves. Negative degrees are zero on both complexes. The definition in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] now makes $\epsilon$ a quasi-isomorphism. The maps whose cohomology was computed are the explicit maps of step 2, so their parameter and coefficient compatibility is the required compatibility. None of the argument identifies these underived complexes with internal right derived invariants.
